newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba sees economy growing 6 to 7 percent in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Cuba sees economy growing 6 to 7 percent in 1996.

text.p: Cuban Vice President Carlos Lage has said that Cuba's economy could grow by up to six or seven percent in 1996 despite damage caused by Hurricane Lili and U.S. efforts to curb foreign investment on the island.

Lage, in remarks broadcast by Cuban television on Saturday night, repeated a prediction that gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year would exceed an official target of five percent originally set by the government.

"It could be six or maybe seven percent," Lage said, adding: "The most important thing is that the forecast (of five percent) is going to be surpassed despite the Helms-Burton law and despite the rise in oil prices."

The Helms-Burton law introduced by the U.S. government in March seeks to curb foreign investment in Cuba by threatening sanctions against investors judged to be "trafficking" in expropriated, formerly U.S.-owned properties on the communist- ruled Caribbean island.

Since Hurricane Lili battered west and central Cuba on Oct. 17 and 18, damaging homes, crops and factories, senior Cuban officials have gone out of their way to stress that the damage, while serious, will not halt Cuba's economic recovery.
